full_judgment: 12. Section 115 of CPC empowers the High Court Division to call for the record of any suit or proceeding in which a decree or an order has been passed by a Court of District Judge or Additional District Judge, or a decree has been passed by a Court of Joint District Judge, Senior Assistant Judge or Assistant Judge, from which no appeal lies. Apart from other limitations placed upon the exercise of that power, one of the essential requirements for the High Court Division to exercise its revisional jurisdiction is that the order sought to be revised must have been made by the aforementioned Courts subordinate to the High Court Division. The Tribunals are meant to deal with only specific class of cases. They do not and cannot exercise powers vested, in a civil court for decision of civil disputes in general within the meaning of section 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Such Tribunals cannot therefore be termed as Civil Courts within the meaning of sections 3, 9 and 115 of the Code.
